AM10G-01.note: 62 - 2(23) = 16. Valid triangle (23,23,16). Distractors are 62/3, 62-23, 62/2. Clean but very easy; early-form item.

AM10G-03.note: clockwise 90: (x,y)->(y,-x) gives (6,4). (-6,-4) is the counterclockwise image, a fair distractor. Direction is stated in caps, so no ambiguity.

AM10G-04.note: P = A + (1/4)(B-A) = (-2+3, 1+2). (4,5) is the midpoint, (7,7) is the 3:1 reversal, (-5,-1) is an external point. Clean.

AM10G-05.note: (10+2w)(24+2w) - 240 = 240 -> 4w^2 + 68w - 240 = 0 -> w^2 + 17w - 60 = 0 -> w = 3. Stem explicitly says OUTSIDE, which removes the usual ambiguity of this family. Requires setting up and solving a quadratic: genuinely late-form.

AM10G-06.note: r = sqrt(5^2+12^2) = 13; (-9,-1) is 13 left of centre. Other options are at distances 12, sqrt(185), 5. Only one is on the circle.

AM10G-07.note: similar cones, linear ratio 1/2, volume ratio 1/8. Point-down orientation is stated, so the water region is the small cone.

AM10G-08.note: d*tan32 = (d-20)*tan47 -> d = 20*tan47/(tan47-tan32) = 47.927; h = 29.948 -> 29.9. Two-angle elevation with a calculator; correctly hard.

AM10G-09.note: diagonal 26 = diameter, r = 13, area 169pi. 676pi uses the diameter as radius, 289pi uses r=17 (10+24 halved? no, 17^2), 26pi is circumference-flavoured. Clean.

AM10G-10.note: horizontal base from (-5,3) to (7,3) is 12; height |3-(-4)| = 7; area 42. 84 is the forgotten 1/2. Clean.

AM10G-11.note: regular hexagon inscribed in r=10 has side 10, perimeter 60. Minor wording oddity: 'to the nearest tenth' is requested for an exactly integral answer, which mildly steers a guesser away from 60.0 toward 69.3/62.8 - harmless, but the rounding instruction is doing no work.

AM10G-12.note: slant height is DEFINED in the stem (apex to midpoint of base edge), which correctly rules out the lateral-edge reading. apothem 6, height sqrt(100-36)=8, V = (1/3)(144)(8) = 384. 1152 omits the 1/3, 480 uses slant height as height.

AM10G-13.note: base 7 (7-24-25), new base 15, new height sqrt(625-225) = 20 (15-20-25). Both triples exact. Clean.

AM10N-03.note: 5(3^6 - 1)/2 = 5*728/2 = 1820. 1215 is the 6th term alone, 3645 the 7th, 364 the sum with a1=1. Clean.

AM10N-04.note: 51/99 = 17/33. 51/990 is the one-digit-offset error, 17/30 a near-miss lookalike. Note 51/990 = 17/330, distinct from every other option.

AM10N-05.note: C(4,2)(2x)^2(-3)^2 = 6*4*9 = 216. 24 drops the (-3)^2, 54 drops the 2^2, 108 drops the binomial coefficient's factor of 2... all fair. Binomial expansion beyond squaring is at the hard end of the ACT.

AM10N-06.note: row1 of A times col2 of B = 2*6 + (-1)(-3) = 15. Correct and unambiguous, but this is the SIXTH matrix-single-entry item in the ACT bank - saturated topic, and the entry chosen (row 1, col 2) is the same shape as the existing five.

AM10N-07.note: <10,-4> - <-3,6> = <13,-10>. The three distractors cover each single sign/scaling slip. Clean.

AM10N-08.note: d = (76-6)/14 = 5; a30 = 6 + 29*5 = 151. 156 is the off-by-one (6+30d), 145 uses 6+29*5 with a1 dropped, 226 uses d=76/14 flavour. Clean.

AM10N-09.note: phi(60) = 60(1/2)(2/3)(4/5) = 16. Edge case n=60: 60/60 is not in lowest terms, correctly excluded; a student who counted it would get 17, which is not an option, so the trap does not resolve to a listed choice - that is the right construction. 44 = 60-16 counts the complement. Genuinely hard for the ACT; coprime counting is rare on the exam but not outside it.

AM10S-01.note: predicted 2.4(12)+15.6 = 44.4; residual 57 - 44.4 = 12.6. Residual is defined in the stem, so the sign convention is not ambiguous and -12.6 is a fair distractor. Clean.

AM10S-02.note: 9*9*8 = 648 favourable of 900; 648/900 = 0.72. 0.648 is the count misread as a probability (out of 1000), which is the intended and effective trap. Counting with a leading-digit restriction is at the hard end.

AM10S-03.note: 20n + 38 = 23(n+1) -> 3n = 15 -> n = 5. 6 is the new-set size, a fair distractor for a misread stem (the stem says ORIGINAL in caps). Clean.
